sections.heading: Why RAG Matters
sections.text: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is the dominant pattern for grounding LLMs in enterprise data. Instead of fine-tuning a model on your data (expensive, stale, hallucination-prone), RAG retrieves relevant documents at query time and injects them into the prompt. This gives you always-fresh knowledge, auditable citations, and zero retraining cost when documents update.
sections.scenario: A banking chatbot must answer questions about 50,000+ policy documents that update weekly. Fine-tuning would require retraining every week at $2,000+ per run with no guarantee the model memorized the right facts. RAG retrieves the exact policy sections in less than 500ms and cites the document ID for auditability.
sections.insight: RAG is not just a cost optimization — it is a compliance requirement in regulated industries. Every answer must trace to a source document with timestamp. Fine-tuned models cannot provide this chain-of-custody.
sections.concept: The RAG formula: Answer = LLM(Query + Retrieved_Context). Quality depends on three factors: (1) retrieval quality — did you find the right documents? (2) context assembly — did you feed the LLM the most relevant chunks? (3) generation quality — did the LLM actually use the context vs hallucinate from parametric memory?
keyPoints: RAG eliminates retraining costs — retrieve instead of memorize
Always-fresh knowledge — documents update, retrieval picks them up instantly
Auditable citations — every claim traces to a source document plus chunk ID
Lower hallucination — LLM answers from provided context, not parametric memory
Fine-tuning is better for: style/tone adaptation, classification, structured extraction
RAG is better for: knowledge-intensive QA, dynamic data, compliance, multi-tenant systems

sections.heading: RAG Architecture Overview
sections.text: RAG architectures evolved from naive retrieve-then-read to sophisticated multi-stage pipelines. The choice depends on your data complexity, query patterns, latency budget, and accuracy requirements.

sections.heading: Chunking Strategies Deep Dive
sections.text: Chunking is the highest-impact preprocessing decision in RAG. Poor chunking breaks context, loses relationships, and tanks retrieval quality.
sections.scenario: A healthcare knowledge base contains clinical guidelines with sections, subsections, tables, and footnotes. Fixed-size chunking at 512 tokens splits a drug dosage table in half, causing the LLM to reference wrong dosages.

code.title: Semantic Chunking with Boundary Detection
code.content:
from langchain_experimental.text_splitter import SemanticChunker
from langchain_openai import OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain.text_splitter import RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter

embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
semantic_splitter = SemanticChunker(
    embeddings,
    breakpoint_threshold_type="percentile",
    breakpoint_threshold_amount=85,
)

docs = load_document("clinical_guidelines.pdf")
semantic_chunks = semantic_splitter.split_documents(docs)
print("Semantic: {} chunks".format(len(semantic_chunks)))

recursive_splitter = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter(
    chunk_size=512, chunk_overlap=50,
    separators=["\n## ", "\n### ", "\n\n", ". ", " "],
)
recursive_chunks = recursive_splitter.split_documents(docs)

def smart_chunk(documents, max_tokens=512):
    chunks = []
    for doc in documents:
        text = doc.page_content
        if "|---|" in text:
            chunks.append(doc)
            continue
        sub_chunks = semantic_splitter.split_documents([doc])
        chunks.extend(sub_chunks)
    return chunks

smart_chunks = smart_chunk(docs)
print("Smart: {} chunks".format(len(smart_chunks)))

sections.heading: Embedding Models Selection
sections.text: Embedding models convert text into dense vector representations for semantic search. The choice impacts retrieval quality, latency, and cost.
sections.insight: Dimension reduction (3072 to 1536) via OpenAI dimensions parameter costs nothing extra and halves storage/compute with less than 1% quality loss.

sections.heading: Vector Database Selection
sections.text: Vector databases store embeddings and perform approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) search. The right choice depends on scale, latency, hybrid search needs, and operational complexity.
sections.scenario: A fintech startup processes 10K documents with hybrid search and metadata filtering. Qdrant in Docker handles this with less than 50ms p95 latency. At 10M documents across 50 tenants, they migrate to Qdrant Cloud cluster.

sections.heading: Hybrid Search with RRF Fusion
sections.text: Pure vector search fails on exact terms like model names, error codes, and IDs. Hybrid search combines dense embeddings (semantic) with sparse BM25 (lexical) via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF).
sections.concept: Reciprocal Rank Fusion merges ranked lists: score(d) = sum(1/(k + rank_i(d))) for each ranking. k=60 is standard. RRF is rank-based not score-based, so it works across different score scales.
sections.warning: Never use raw cosine similarity + BM25 scores directly — they are on different scales. Always use RRF or z-score normalization.

code.title: Hybrid Search with RRF (Qdrant Native)
code.content:
from qdrant_client import QdrantClient
from qdrant_client.models import DenseVector, SparseVector, Prefetch, Query, FusionQuery

class HybridSearchEngine:
    def __init__(self, collection="knowledge_base"):
        self.client = QdrantClient("localhost", port=6333)
        self.collection = collection

    def search(self, query_text, dense_vector, sparse_vector, top_k=10):
        results = self.client.query_points(
            collection_name=self.collection,
            query=Query(
                prefetch=[
                    Prefetch(query=DenseVector(name="text-embedding-3-small", vector=dense_vector), limit=top_k*3),
                    Prefetch(query=SparseVector(name="bm25", indices=sparse_vector["indices"], values=sparse_vector["values"]), limit=top_k*3),
                ],
                fusion=FusionQuery(rrf=True),
            ),
            limit=top_k, with_payload=True,
        )
        return [{"id": h.id, "score": h.score, "text": h.payload.get("text","")} for h in results.points]

engine = HybridSearchEngine()
results = engine.search("GPT-4o pricing enterprise", dense_vec, sparse_vec, top_k=10)

sections.heading: Reranking — The Highest-ROI Step
sections.text: Reranking is the single highest-ROI improvement in a RAG pipeline. A cross-encoder reranker re-scores top-K retrieved chunks. This improves top-3 recall by 15-30% with only 50-200ms additional latency.
sections.insight: Without reranking, your RAG is leaving 15-30% of relevant answers on the table. It is the cheapest quality improvement you can make.

sections.heading: Query Capture and Logging
sections.text: Every query must be logged with full traceability for debugging, compliance, and improvement. In regulated industries, query logging is a compliance requirement.

code.title: Query Capture with Full Traceability
code.content:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, asdict
import uuid, datetime, logging

logger = logging.getLogger("rag.query")

@dataclass
class QueryLog:
    query_id: str
    raw_text: str
    user_id: str
    session_id: str
    timestamp: str
    metadata: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
    domain: str = None
    embedding_time_ms: float = 0
    retrieval_time_ms: float = 0
    grounding_score: float = 0
    citations: list = field(default_factory=list)

def capture_query(text, user_id, session_id, domain=None):
    log = QueryLog(
        query_id=str(uuid.uuid4())[:12],
        raw_text=text, user_id=user_id, session_id=session_id,
        timestamp=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        domain=domain,
        metadata={"char_count": len(text), "word_count": len(text.split())}
    )
    logger.info("Query captured: {}".format(log.query_id))
    return log

sections.text: Raw queries are almost never optimal for retrieval. Query processing includes rewriting for clarity, decomposition into sub-queries, and HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings) for bridging the vocabulary gap.
sections.concept: HyDE generates a hypothetical answer first, then embeds that answer for retrieval. This bridges the gap between short queries and rich documents, improving recall by 10-20%.

sections.heading: Generation with Citations
sections.text: Generate the final answer using the assembled context. The prompt must instruct the LLM to answer ONLY from the provided context and cite sources.
sections.warning: If the LLM cannot find the answer in the context, it should say I do not have enough information — NOT guess.

code.title: Grounded Generation with Citation Extraction
code.content:
from openai import OpenAI
import re

client = OpenAI()

SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are a helpful assistant.
RULES:
1. Answer ONLY using the provided context.
2. Every claim must cite a source using [N] format.
3. If context is insufficient, say so.
4. Never fabricate citations."""

def generate_answer(query, context, sources, domain="general"):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o",
        messages=[
            {"role": "system", "content": SYSTEM_PROMPT},
            {"role": "user", "content": "Context:\n{}\n\nQuestion: {}".format(context, query)}
        ],
        temperature=0.1, max_tokens=2000,
    )
    answer = response.choices[0].message.content
    citations_used = list(set(re.findall(r'\[(\d+)\]', answer)))
    return {
        "answer": answer,
        "citations": [sources[int(c)-1] for c in citations_used if int(c) <= len(sources)],
        "tokens_used": response.usage.total_tokens,
    }

sections.heading: Grounding Verification
sections.text: Verify that the generated answer is grounded in the retrieved context. Without this, the LLM may hallucinate facts not in your knowledge base.
sections.scenario: A healthcare RAG system generates Drug X should not be taken with alcohol but the context only says Consult your physician. The grounding check catches this unsupported claim.

code.title: Grounding Verification with LLM-as-Judge
code.content:
from openai import OpenAI
import json

client = OpenAI()

def verify_grounding(answer, context):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": 'Analyze answer against context. For each claim: SUPPORTED, PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED. Return JSON: {"overall_score": 0.0-1.0, "recommendation": PASS|WARN|FAIL}'},
                   {"role": "user", "content": "Context:\n{}\n\nAnswer:\n{}".format(context, answer)}],
        temperature=0.1, response_format={"type": "json_object"},
    )
    result = json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)
    if result.get("overall_score", 0) < 0.7:
        result["recommendation"] = "FAIL"
    return result

sections.heading: Corrective RAG (CRAG)
sections.text: CRAG adds a self-correction loop. After retrieval, a grader evaluates relevance. If not relevant enough, the system performs web search or deeper retrieval.
sections.concept: The CRAG loop: Retrieve then Grade. If relevant: extract and generate. If partially relevant: extract key plus web search. If irrelevant: web search only.

code.title: CRAG Implementation with Relevance Grading
code.content:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from typing import TypedDict

class CRAGState(TypedDict):
    query: str
    documents: list
    grade: str
    answer: str

def retrieve(state):
    docs = vector_store.search(state["query"], top_k=5)
    return {"documents": docs}

def grade_relevance(state):
    response = client.chat.completions.create(
        model="gpt-4o-mini",
        messages=[{"role": "system", "content": "Grade as relevant, partially_relevant, or irrelevant."},
                   {"role": "user", "content": "Q: {} Docs: {}".format(state["query"], [d["text"][:200] for d in state["documents"]]) }],
        response_format={"type": "json_object"},
    )
    return json.loads(response.choices[0].message.content)

def route_relevance(state):
    if state["grade"] == "relevant": return "generate"
    return "generate"

def generate(state):
    context = "\n".join(d["text"] for d in state["documents"])
    response = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Context: {}\nQ: {}".format(context, state["query"]) }])
    return {"answer": response.choices[0].message.content}

graph = StateGraph(CRAGState)
graph.add_node("retrieve", retrieve)
graph.add_node("grade", grade_relevance)
graph.add_node("generate", generate)
graph.set_entry_point("retrieve")
graph.add_edge("retrieve", "grade")
graph.add_conditional_edges("grade", route_relevance, {"generate": "generate"})
graph.add_edge("generate", END)
app = graph.compile()

code.content:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, Settings
from llama_index.llms.openai import OpenAI
from llama_index.core.query_engine import RouterQueryEngine
from llama_index.core.tools import QueryEngineTool
from llama_index.core.selectors import PydanticSingleSelector
from llama_index.readers.file import PDFReader

Settings.llm = OpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0)
Settings.chunk_size = 512

docs = PDFReader().load_data("./policy_documents/")
vector_index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)
summary_index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(docs)

vector_tool = QueryEngineTool.from_defaults(query_engine=vector_index.as_query_engine(), description="Factual questions")
summary_tool = QueryEngineTool.from_defaults(query_engine=summary_index.as_query_engine(response_mode="tree_summarize"), description="Summary questions")

router = RouterQueryEngine(selector=PydanticSingleSelector.from_defaults(), query_engine_tools=[vector_tool, summary_tool])
response = router.query("What are the key changes in the 2024 policy update?")
print(response)

code.title: LangChain LCEL RAG Chain with Streaming
code.content:
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI, OpenAIEmbeddings
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import StrOutputParser
from langchain_core.runnables import RunnablePassthrough, RunnableParallel
from langchain_qdrant import QdrantVectorStore

llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0, streaming=True)
embeddings = OpenAIEmbeddings(model="text-embedding-3-small")
vector_store = QdrantVectorStore.from_existing_collection(embedding=embeddings, collection_name="knowledge_base", url="http://localhost:6333")
retriever = vector_store.as_retriever(search_kwargs={"k": 5})

prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template("""Context: {context}

Question: {question}

Answer based ONLY on context. Cite [N].""")

def format_docs(docs): return "\n\n".join("[{}] {}".format(i+1, d.page_content) for i, d in enumerate(docs))

rag_chain = (
    RunnableParallel(context=retriever | format_docs, question=RunnablePassthrough())
    | prompt | llm | StrOutputParser()
)

for chunk in rag_chain.stream("What is the refund policy?"):
    print(chunk, end="", flush=True)

code.title: Main Application Entry Point
code.content:
# app/main.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from app.rag.pipeline import RAGPipeline
from app.rag.guardrails import RAGGuardrails
from app.config import settings

pipeline = None
guardrails = None

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    global pipeline, guardrails
    pipeline = RAGPipeline(collection=settings.QDRANT_COLLECTION, embedding_model=settings.EMBEDDING_MODEL, llm_model=settings.LLM_MODEL)
    guardrails = RAGGuardrails()
    yield
    pipeline.close()

app = FastAPI(title="RAG API", lifespan=lifespan)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_methods=["*"])

@app.post("/api/chat")
async def chat(request: ChatRequest):
    input_check = guardrails.check_input(request.message)
    if not input_check["safe"]:
        return {"error": "Query blocked", "reason": input_check["reason"]}
    result = await pipeline.run(query=request.message, user_id=request.user_id, tenant_id=request.tenant_id)
    output_check = guardrails.check_output(result["answer"])
    if not output_check["safe"]:
        result["answer"] = "[Response filtered for compliance]"
    return result

@app.get("/api/health")
async def health():
    return {"status": "healthy", "version": "1.0.0"}

sections.heading: What Are AI Agents
sections.text: AI agents are autonomous systems that use LLMs as their reasoning engine to plan, decide, and execute actions. Unlike simple prompt-response chains, agents maintain state, use tools, and adapt their approach based on intermediate results.
sections.concept: The Agent Loop: Perceive -> Think -> Act -> Observe -> Repeat. The LLM decides: (1) what tool to call, (2) with what arguments, (3) whether the result is sufficient or more action is needed.
keyPoints: Agents are not chatbots — they are goal-oriented autonomous systems
Tools extend the LLM beyond text generation to real-world actions
Memory enables context retention across steps and sessions
Planning breaks complex goals into manageable sub-tasks
Guardrails prevent unwanted actions and ensure safe operation

sections.heading: Agent Architecture Patterns
sections.text: Different agent architectures serve different use cases. Choose based on complexity, reliability needs, and human oversight requirements.

sections.heading: Building Agents with LangGraph
sections.text: LangGraph provides a state-graph framework for building deterministic agents. Unlike chain-based approaches, LangGraph gives you explicit control over state, branching, and loops.

code.title: ReAct Agent with LangGraph
code.content:
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolNode
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.messages import HumanMessage, SystemMessage
from typing import TypedDict, Annotated, List
from langchain_core.messages import BaseMessage
import operator


class AgentState(TypedDict):
    messages: Annotated[List[BaseMessage], operator.add]
    next: str


llm = ChatOpenAI(model="gpt-4o", temperature=0)
tools = [search_web, query_database, send_email]
llm_with_tools = llm.bind_tools(tools)


def agent_node(state):
    response = llm_with_tools.invoke(state["messages"])
    return {"messages": [response]}


def tool_node(state):
    tool_node = ToolNode(tools)
    return tool_node.invoke(state)


def should_continue(state):
    last_message = state["messages"][-1]
    if hasattr(last_message, "tool_calls") and last_message.tool_calls:
        return "tools"
    return END


graph = StateGraph(AgentState)
graph.add_node("agent", agent_node)
graph.add_node("tools", tool_node)
graph.set_entry_point("agent")
graph.add_conditional_edges("agent", should_continue, {"tools": "tools", END: END})
graph.add_edge("tools", "agent")
app = graph.compile()


result = app.invoke({"messages": [SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful agent."), HumanMessage(content="Find the latest sales data and summarize.")]})

sections.heading: EU AI Act — Risk Classification Engine
sections.text: The EU AI Act requires every AI system to be classified by risk level. This engine automates classification so you can instantly determine obligations for any AI system you build.

code.title: EU AI Act Risk Classification (Python)
code.content:
from enum import Enum
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional


class RiskLevel(Enum):
    UNACCEPTABLE = "unacceptable"
    HIGH = "high"
    LIMITED = "limited"
    MINIMAL = "minimal"


class AIRiskClassifier:
    """EU AI Act Art. 6-51 automated risk classification."""
    
    # Annex III: High-risk areas
    HIGH_RISK_AREAS = [
        "biometric identification", "critical infrastructure",
        "education", "employment", "credit scoring",
        "law enforcement", "migration", "justice"
    ]
    
    UNACCEPTABLE_AREAS = [
        "social scoring", "real-time biometric surveillance",
        "exploiting vulnerabilities", "manipulative AI"
    ]
    
    def classify(self, system: dict) -> dict:
        purpose = system.get("purpose", "").lower()
        area = system.get("area", "").lower()
        
        if any(u in area for u in self.UNACCEPTABLE_AREAS):
            return {"level": RiskLevel.UNACCEPTABLE, "obligations": ["PROHIBITED"]}
        if any(h in area for h in self.HIGH_RISK_AREAS):
            obligations = [
                "Conformity assessment (Art. 43)",
                "Register in EU database (Art. 49)",
                "DPIA required (Art. 35 GDPR)",
                "Human oversight (Art. 14)",
                "Technical documentation (Art. 11)",
                "Risk management system (Art. 9)",
                "Data governance (Art. 10)",
                "Transparency (Art. 13)",
                "Accuracy, robustness, cybersecurity (Art. 15)"
            ]
            return {"level": RiskLevel.HIGH, "obligations": obligations}
        if purpose in ["chatbot", "deepfake", "emotion recognition"]:
            return {"level": RiskLevel.LIMITED, "obligations": ["Transparency: label AI-generated content"]}
        return {"level": RiskLevel.MINIMAL, "obligations": ["Voluntary code of conduct (Art. 95)"]}
    
    def generate_technical_doc(self, system: dict) -> str:
        """Generate Art. 11 technical documentation template."""
        return f"""# EU AI Act Technical Documentation
## System: {system.get('name', 'Unnamed')}
### 1. General description
- Purpose: {system.get('purpose')}
- Input data: {system.get('input_type')}
- Output: {system.get('output_type')}
### 2. Development methodology
- Training data provenance: [document]
- Model architecture: [describe]
- Training setup: [hyperparameters]
### 3. Risk management
- Identified risks: [list]
- Mitigations: [list]
- Residual risk: [accept/reduce/transfer]
### 4. Human oversight measures
- Oversight mechanism: [describe]
- Override capability: [yes/no]
### 5. Accuracy & robustness
- Performance metrics: [list]
- Robustness testing: [adversarial, edge cases]
"""

sections.heading: ISO 42001 — AI Management System (AIMS)
sections.text: ISO 42001 provides the international standard framework for AI management systems. Certification demonstrates regulatory preparedness. Below is a complete AIMS implementation with policy templates, control tracking, and audit automation.

code.title: ISO 42001 AIMS Implementation Toolkit
code.content:
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from typing import List, Optional


@dataclass
class AIMSControl:
    domain: str
    control_id: str
    description: str
    status: str = "not_implemented"
    evidence: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    owner: str = ""
    due_date: Optional[str] = None


class AIMS:
    """ISO 42001 AI Management System."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.controls: List[AIMSControl] = []
        self.policies = {}
    
    def add_policy(self, name: str, content: str):
        self.policies[name] = {
            "content": content,
            "approved_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
            "version": "1.0"
        }
    
    def create_default_policies(self):
        self.add_policy("AI Governance Policy", """
# AI Governance Policy
## Scope
Applies to all AI systems developed or deployed by the organization.
## Principles
1. Human oversight: All high-risk AI decisions must have human review.
2. Transparency: All AI interactions must be disclosed to users.
3. Fairness: Bias testing required before deployment.
4. Accountability: Each model must have a named owner.
5. Privacy: Data minimization and PII protection mandatory.
## Governance Structure
- AI Ethics Board: quarterly review of high-risk systems
- Model Review Board: pre-deployment approval
- Data Council: data quality and lineage oversight
## Enforcement
Non-compliance triggers corrective action plan within 30 days.
""")
        self.add_policy("Data Governance Policy", """
# Data Governance Policy for AI
## Data Classification
- Public: external non-sensitive data
- Internal: business data, no PII
- Confidential: PII, financial, health data
- Restricted: highly sensitive, regulated
## Data Lifecycle
1. Collection: consent obtained, purpose stated
2. Storage: encrypted at rest, access-controlled
3. Processing: purpose-limited, retention-bounded
4. Deletion: automated after retention period
## Training Data Requirements
- Provenance documented for all datasets
- Bias assessment required before training
- Consent verified for all personal data
""")
    
    def add_control(self, control: AIMSControl):
        self.controls.append(control)
    
    def readiness_score(self) -> dict:
        """Calculate certification readiness."""
        total = len(self.controls)
        implemented = sum(1 for c in self.controls if c.status == "implemented")
        verified = sum(1 for c in self.controls if len(c.evidence) > 0)
        return {
            "total_controls": total,
            "implemented": implemented,
            "with_evidence": verified,
            "readiness_pct": round(implemented / total * 100, 1) if total else 0,
            "gap_areas": [c.control_id for c in self.controls if c.status == "not_implemented"]
        }

sections.heading: GDPR — DPIA Automation & Art. 22 Compliance
sections.text: GDPR Art. 22 restricts solely automated decision-making with legal effects. Combined with Art. 35 (DPIA), this is the most common AI compliance gap. Below is an automated DPIA generator and Art. 22 compliance checker.

code.title: GDPR DPIA Automation Engine
code.content:
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import List, Optional


class DPIARiskLevel:
    LOW = "low"
    MEDIUM = "medium"
    HIGH = "high"


@dataclass
class DPIAResponse:
    question_id: str
    answer: str
    risk_indicators: List[str]


class DPIAAutomation:
    """Automated Data Protection Impact Assessment (Art. 35)."""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.questions = [
            {"id": "Q1", "text": "Does the AI process sensitive data (health, biometrics, genetics)?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 9, Art. 35"},
            {"id": "Q2", "text": "Does the AI make automated decisions with legal effects?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 22"},
            {"id": "Q3", "text": "Does the AI profile vulnerable individuals (children, elderly)?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 35, Recital 75"},
            {"id": "Q4", "text": "Does the AI process data on a large scale?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 35(3)"},
            {"id": "Q5", "text": "Does the AI involve systematic monitoring of individuals?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 35(3), Recital 91"},
            {"id": "Q6", "text": "Is the AI used for credit scoring or eligibility decisions?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 22, Recital 71"},
            {"id": "Q7", "text": "Does the AI combine data from multiple sources in novel ways?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 35"},
            {"id": "Q8", "text": "Does the AI exclude individuals from services or benefits?",
             "high_risk": ["yes"], "gdpr_article": "Art. 22(4)"},
        ]
        self.responses: List[DPIAResponse] = []
    
    def assess(self, answers: dict) -> dict:
        high_risk_triggers = []
        for q in self.questions:
            ans = answers.get(q["id"], "").lower()
            if ans in q["high_risk"]:
                high_risk_triggers.append(q)
        
        is_high_risk = len(high_risk_triggers) >= 2
        return {
            "dpia_required": is_high_risk,
            "risk_level": "HIGH" if is_high_risk else "LOW",
            "triggers": [t["id"] + ": " + t["gdpr_article"] for t in high_risk_triggers],
            "articles": list(set(t["gdpr_article"] for t in high_risk_triggers)),
            "recommendations": [
                "Conduct full DPIA immediately" if is_high_risk else "DPIA recommended but not mandatory",
                "Document processing purpose and legal basis (Art. 5, 6)",
                "Implement human-in-the-loop for automated decisions (Art. 22)",
                "Provide right to explanation mechanism (Recital 71)",
                "Register processing activity in ROPA (Art. 30)"
            ]
        }
    
    def generate_dpia_report(self, answers: dict, system_info: dict) -> str:
        assessment = self.assess(answers)
        return f"""# Data Protection Impact Assessment
## System: {system_info.get('name', 'Unnamed')}
### Risk Classification: {assessment['risk_level']}
### Articles triggered: {', '.join(assessment['articles'])}
### Processing Description
- Purpose: {system_info.get('purpose')}
- Data categories: {system_info.get('data_categories')}
- Data subjects: {system_info.get('data_subjects')}
- Retention period: {system_info.get('retention')}
### Necessity & Proportionality Assessment
[Assess whether processing is necessary and proportionate]
### Risk Assessment
[Describe risks to rights and freedoms]
### Mitigation Measures
{chr(10).join('- ' + r for r in assessment['recommendations'])}
### Data Protection Officer Review
[DPO name, date]
### Review Date: [90 days from today]
"""

code.content:
import json
from typing import List, Dict, Callable
from enum import Enum


class PolicyResult(Enum):
    ALLOW = "allow"
    DENY = "deny"
    REVIEW = "review"
    NOTIFY = "notify"


class PolicyRule:
    def __init__(self, name: str, evaluate: Callable[[dict], PolicyResult],
                 description: str = "", framework: str = "", severity: str = "medium"):
        self.name = name
        self.evaluate = evaluate
        self.description = description
        self.framework = framework
        self.severity = severity


class GovernancePolicyEngine:
    def __init__(self):
        self.rules: List[PolicyRule] = []
    
    def add_default_rules(self):
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "no_social_scoring",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if "social scoring" in m.get("purpose", "").lower() else PolicyResult.ALLOW,
            "Social scoring systems are prohibited under EU AI Act", "EU AI Act", "critical"
        ))
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "human_oversight_high_risk",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if m.get("risk_level") == "high" and not m.get("human_in_the_loop") else PolicyResult.ALLOW,
            "High-risk AI systems require human oversight", "EU AI Act", "critical"
        ))
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "model_card_required",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if not m.get("model_card") else PolicyResult.ALLOW,
            "All models must have a model card", "ISO 42001", "high"
        ))
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "bias_testing",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if m.get("risk_level") in ["high", "medium"] and not m.get("bias_tested") else PolicyResult.ALLOW,
            "Bias testing required for medium/high risk", "NIST AI RMF", "high"
        ))
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "pii_masking",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if m.get("has_pii") and not m.get("pii_masked") else PolicyResult.ALLOW,
            "PII must be masked before LLM inference", "GDPR", "critical"
        ))
        self.rules.append(PolicyRule(
            "data_retention",
            lambda m: PolicyResult.DENY if m.get("retention_days", 365) > 90 and m.get("data_type") == "personal" else PolicyResult.NOTIFY,
            "Personal data retention should not exceed 90 days", "GDPR/PDPA", "medium"
        ))
    
    def evaluate_all(self, manifest: dict) -> dict:
        results = []
        for rule in self.rules:
            try:
                result = rule.evaluate(manifest)
            except Exception as e:
                result = PolicyResult.REVIEW
            results.append({
                "rule": rule.name,
                "result": result.value,
                "framework": rule.framework,
                "severity": rule.severity,
                "description": rule.description
            })
        
        denied = [r for r in results if r["result"] == "deny"]
        return {
            "manifest": manifest.get("name", "unknown"),
            "overall": "DENIED" if denied else "APPROVED",
            "blocking_rules": denied,
            "warnings": [r for r in results if r["result"] in ["review", "notify"]],
            "passed": len([r for r in results if r["result"] == "allow"]),
            "total": len(results)
        }
